scope: Eqs. (4), (8), (11). In the computational basis each two-site flip has a unique bond mask. Making all couplings nonnegative replaces every entry of −H and every spin-flip path weight by its exact absolute value.
Eq. (10). Walsh characters are signs. On a two-site mask the character is the product of the two classical Ising spins, so the absolute integer energy is bounded by the number of occupied bonds.
Eq. (11). The signed quantum Hamiltonian is exactly the sum of the two-site Pauli X flip matrices multiplied by −Jₑ, with couplings 0, ±1 in units of J.
Eq. (4) and Fig. 2. A four-site square with one negative bond has a concrete length-four closed spin-flip path of unscaled weight −1. The same bosonic path has weight +1.
Eqs. (10)–(11). The Walsh basis gives an invertible change of basis from the matrix of signed two-site flips to the diagonal matrix of classical energies. This retains all eigenvalue multiplicities.
Eqs. (3), (10)–(11). The quantum mean Tr[H exp(−βH)]/Tr[exp(−βH)] computed with the matrix exponential equals the Gibbs-weighted mean of the classical spin-glass energies for every real β.

Paragraph after Eq. (10). The finite energy minimum exists. Shifting to one ground configuration keeps the Gibbs mean, yields a partition sum at least one, and bounds all integer excitation energies by twice the bond count.
Paragraph after Eq. (10). For N spins with integer excitation energies in [0,D], D>0 and β≥0, the finite-temperature energy exceeds the minimum by less than 2ᴺ D exp(−β).

Paragraph after Eq. (10), energy unit J=1. For N>0, at most 3N occupied bonds and β≥N log 2+log(12N), a ground energy ≤t implies thermal mean <t+1/2. Otherwise the thermal mean is ≥t+1. The non-strict NO endpoint includes flat spectra and gives the required decision gap. For physical coupling J>0, the proof scales the temperature as βJ and the energy window as J/2.
Paragraph after Eq. (10). An inverse temperature β=13N in units J=1 satisfies the published logarithmic lower bound for every positive spin count.
Eq. (9) and the reduction after Eq. (10). The absolute thermal energy is bounded by the number of occupied bonds, converting an inverse-linear relative error target into constant absolute error.

Eq. (9) and note [9]. A single signed-energy estimate at β=13N with relative root mean squared error ≤1/(24N) decides the integer threshold with failure probability ≤1/4 over any probability space. This implication concerns the spin-glass decision problem; an NP-class reduction is additional.
After Eq. (11). All-aligned spins attain energy −m for m nonzero ferromagnetic bonds, and this is a ground configuration.

Sign-free comparison after Eq. (11), restricted to the thermal decision query. At β=13N, returning the negative number of occupied bonds deterministically estimates the bosonic mean to relative error ≤1/(24N). The zero-bond case is exact. No mixing-time hypothesis is needed for this query.
Eq. (10). In an open three-dimensional box of size a×b×c there are at most three positive-direction nearest-neighbour bonds per vertex, with boundary self-edges excluded.

Eqs. (8)–(11), note [9]. For an explicit three-dimensional lattice with couplings 0, ±1, one signed thermal estimate gives a bounded-error ground-threshold decision. At exactly its temperature and tolerance the bosonic comparison is computed by the occupied-bond count. Barahona’s NP-hardness result, uniform machine complexity and all-temperature cluster mixing are separate claims.

Eq. (4). For each integer k≥0 the closed paths with k+1 transitions sum to the signed trace Taylor coefficient β^(k+1) Tr[(−H)^(k+1)]/(k+1)!. Including the trace of the identity at order zero, the complete series converges to Tr[exp(−βH)].

Eqs. (6)–(8). At nonnegative β the ferromagnetic Taylor weights are exactly the absolute signed weights. At any order of nonzero signed mass the signed observable mean is recovered by the ratio of two bosonic expectations.
